reviewedAreas: Qualification history and preservation of conclusive receipts across transient probes
BlockRun anonymous transport, exact-zero admission, current catalog and served-model identity
Provider-specific policy receipts, public-code privacy, source-IP quota ownership
Static Windows package file inclusion for Puter and BlockRun modules

findings.impact: Active in-memory receipt reads shared their object with archived history, allowing caller mutation to alter successful historical evidence.
findings.repair: Active read methods return structured clones; mutation-isolation regression passes. SQLite deserialization already returned independent values.

findings.impact: An executable tool completion could be emitted before a later usage frame rejected a substituted model identity.
findings.repair: BlockRun buffers executable tool completions and finish until the underlying checked stream ends successfully; errors discard buffered actions.

facts: Current model availability and explicit free billing/zero input-output prices required before dispatch.
No credential, wallet or payment headers sent; payment challenges are not satisfied and redirects are not followed.
Substituted/missing model identities cannot produce executable tool completions through the reviewed BlockRun wrapper.
A provider-specific current policy receipt and qualified role remain required by the Free supply fabric.
BlockRun direct supply uses the existing public-code-only/consent boundary.
Provider promises concerning its own prompt retention do not establish every upstream's private-code guarantees.
Source-IP route counts remain finite and shared across users/models; underlying NVIDIA capacity is also shared.

windowsInclusion.limit: Final frozen ASAR content/hash and signing audits remain the delivery workstream's responsibility.
